t: You are looking at St Mary-le-Bow, a Church of England parish church on Cheapside, one of the City's oldest streets. The church was founded in 1080 by Lanfranc, Archbishop of Canterbury, and it has been rebuilt several times. The present building is by Sir Christopher Wren, after the Great Fire of 1666. Its tall spire is still a City landmark. Among Wren's churches, only St Paul's Cathedral and St Bride's, Fleet Street, are taller. It cost over £15,000, his second most expensive building after St Paul's.
